title: candidate mental map + risk grid — Meera Shah
content:
Quick personal synthesis for Meera Shah (senior runtime engineer, onsite loop 2026-02-17) — raw sketch for handoff to hiring chair. Notes to self: treat as private until I’ve cleaned up.

Context and role fit hypothesis:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference serving runtime team). Expectation: systems-level performance work, kernel tradeoffs, infra collaboration, production debugging.
- Meera's background: 6y production infra at a mid-stage ML infra company, shipped a custom batching layer and a latency-aware router. Strong pragmatic optimization instincts, less exposure to deep kernel-level compiler work but shows eagerness to learn.

Interview highlights (verbatim impressions + summary):
- System design exercise (20m): proposed a tiered router with token-level batching windows. Good on SLO reasoning; sketched cache invalidation edgecases.
- Live coding (30m): implemented a simplified prefix-cache API; had a small bug in concurrency path but found and explained fix quickly.
- Deep dive (40m): asked clarifying questions about kernel/quantization tradeoffs; candid about unknowns.

Quick numeric gut-check (0–4 scale):
- Core infra engineering (concurrency, networking): 3
- LLM-specific inference intuition (KV cache, batching): 3
- Low-level optimization / CUDA / compilers: 2
- System design & tradeoff communication: 4
- Debugging under pressure: 3

Mental map (how Meera thinks about problems):
- Tends to break problems into three layers: request shaping (client + router), batching/caching layer, GPU execution.
- Prioritizes predictable tail-latency over microbatch throughput in most designs.
- Defaults to simple, observable heuristics (e.g., latency windows, token budget) rather than heavy ML scheduling.

Risk grid (probability vs impact + suggested mitigations) — quick matrix:
- Risk: Limited low-level kernel expertise. Probability: medium. Impact: medium-high for deep optimization projects. Mitigation: pair with compiler team, 3-month ramp focusing on profiling and small kernel audits; assign a mentor on applied-ml.
- Risk: Openness to shipping tradeoffs that favor reliability might slow aggressive perf wins. Probability: low-medium. Impact: medium. Mitigation: frame initial objectives around shipping perf experiments that preserve reliability metrics; timebox experiments.
- Risk: Unfamiliarity with our deployment patterns (Dedicated / Private). Probability: medium. Impact: medium. Mitigation: short rotation shadowing SRE + private-deploy onboarding checklist.
- Risk: Ownership friction when collaborating across product teams. Probability: low. Impact: low-medium. Mitigation: explicit cross-team SLA doc and shared dashboards during first quarter.

Behavioral & culture signals: 
- Communicates clearly, good at surfacing assumptions.
- Shows humility; asks for clarifying context rather than guessing.
- Seems motivated by shipping reliable systems rather than heroics.

Open questions / follow-ups I want to capture for committee:
1) Depth check: give a short take-home microtask to inspect a hot path profile and write 3 short suggestions (should reveal kernel intuition).
2) Pair session with an infra engineer who has done quantized model rollouts at Redwood (expose gaps quickly).
3) Verify experience with specific stacks we use: Triton/torchscript/ONNX runtime. Ask for concrete examples.

Recommended ask for leveling / IC band: Senior (IC3) with performance stretch goals. Consider hiring leveled to Senior with a growth plan for low-level optimization competency.

Decision lean (my current vote): Strong hire with a 1:1 follow-up microtask and a recommended mentor pairing during the first 90 days.

Snippets to copy into panel debrief: 
- "Clear systems thinker, pragmatic in tradeoffs, strong at designing for tail-latency and observability."
- "Needs ramp on kernel-level optimization; good learner and explains thought process."

Action items (next 72h):
- Send candidate a short profiling microtask + 72h deadline (I can author). Linked to JIRA-ENG-4821.
- Slack Ravi + Sofia to schedule a 90-min pairing if microtask looks promising.
- Draft onboarding checklist for Dedicated/Private exposure (quick wins for first 30 days).

Raw scratchnotes (time-stamped):
- 02:20am: noted candidate used the phrase 'latency-safe batching' — good sign of product-aware thinking.
- 02:45am: candidate mentioned previous outages: root cause was a poorly sized batch window colliding with request bursts; they implemented adaptive backoff — ask for postmortem later.

Notes-to-self: keep doc private, move into shared 'hiring' folder once microtask validated.

End.
